author: A. Cunningham
evidence: The Taxila copper plate of the satrap Liaka Kusuluka, found at Thupkia in the middle of Sirsukh, names him satrap of Chhahara and Chukhsa north-east of the city of Takhasila; since Sirsukh lies NE of Sirkap, Sirkap must be Taxila and Sirsukh Chhahara.
quote: this copper-plate was found in the village of Thupkia, in the middle of the ruined city of Sir-sukh
note: Index gap noted in FOLLOWUPS (ASR V pp. 67–68). Bears on the city of the 1st c. BC/AD, not directly on the capital of Xuanzang's day.

author: A. Cunningham
asr_identification: Hatial, the lower half of Sur-garh hill at Taxila (Cunningham)
evidence: Cunningham reads Songyun's "body" as "head" and puts the head-gift scene at Taxila, below the fortified hill of Sur-garh, whose lower slope is called Hatial or Athial, "place of bones".
quote: the lofty fortified hill of Sur-garh, with its precipices, overlooks the ancient city
note: Rival to Mizutani's Bhallar stūpa; rests on the place-name.
